results.content: # AI Evaluation Metrics - Precision. Precision is the proportion of true positive results among all positive predictions made by the AI model. In simpler terms, it measures how often the AI's positive advice or recommendations are actually relevant and correct. Reduce false positives—e.g., avoid recommending irrelevant or potentially harmful products or advice, which can lead to user mistrust or safety issues. **Set Precision Thresholds:** Define acceptable precision levels (e.g., ≥ 80% for wellness, ≥ 93% for pharmacies). **Review False Positives:** Regularly audit AI outputs to identify and document cases where the AI gave incorrect positive recommendations. **User Feedback Loop:** Implement mechanisms for users to flag irrelevant or inappropriate advice to feed into precision improvement. **Compliance Reporting:** Report precision metrics in compliance documentation and track improvements over time. **Error Analysis:** Analyze false positives systematically to identify common causes and update model or data accordingly. #### AI Evaluation Metrics - Recall (Sensitivity). #### AI Evaluation Metrics - Accuracy. results.content: # 7 Proven Techniques for Optimizing Precision-Recall Curve Area. 7 Proven Techniques for Optimizing Precision-Recall Curve Area. In this article, we will explore seven proven techniques to optimize the Area Under the Precision-Recall Curve (AUPRC). The Precision-Recall (PR) Curve is a powerful tool in evaluating the performance of classification models, particularly when dealing with datasets that have an imbalance between the classes. * **Overfitting:** Like any other metric, excessive optimization on training data can lead to models that perform exceptionally well on the PR Curve during training but fail to generalize to unseen data. By creating a more balanced dataset, the model is better positioned to learn distinct features of the minority class, thus improving both precision and recall. Mathematically, if θ is the threshold value, the performance of the model might be optimized by solving:. This calibration is especially crucial for models where the balance of precision and recall is pivotal. Ensemble methods can smooth out individual model inconsistencies and provide a more robust prediction, making them a powerful tool for AUPRC optimization. Regularization techniques penalize overly complex models, encouraging them to learn more general features. A well-regularized and tuned model is less likely to exhibit extreme behavior on either precision or recall, thereby achieving a more balanced and higher AUPRC. By calibrating your model effectively, you ensure that the decision thresholds you set truly correspond to meaningful changes in precision and recall. After a model has been trained and calibrated, post-hoc evaluation and analysis can further enhance performance. * Calibrate the model using techniques like Platt scaling directly from scikit-learn’s `CalibratedClassifierCV`. Optimizing the AUPRC is a multifaceted endeavor that requires careful attention to data handling, model calibration, and post-hoc analysis. While implementing these techniques, be prepared to face challenges such as noisy data, model overfitting, and variability in performance metrics. By applying the seven techniques detailed in this article, you can significantly enhance your model’s ability to correctly identify positive instances, thereby optimizing the AUPRC. Remember, the key lies in a systematic approach: start with data rebalancing, move through feature engineering and aggressive model calibration, and finally, iterate based on rigorous post-hoc analysis.

results.title: Evaluation metrics for object detection and segmentation: mAP
results.content: # Evaluation metrics for object detection and segmentation: mAP. ## Precision and Recall. **Precision** is the Positive prediction value i.e. Of all the positive predictions, how many are True positives predictions. Now, calculate the precision and recall e.g. for P4, `Precision = 1/(1+0) = 1`, and `Recall = 1/3 = 0.33`. The AP summarizes the shape of the precision-recall curve, and, in **VOC 2007**, it is defined as the mean of precision values at a set of 11 equally spaced recall levels [0,0.1,…,1] (0 to 1 at step size of 0.1), *not the AUC*. i.e. take the max precision value to the right at 11 equally spaced recall points [0: 0.1: 1], and take their mean to get AP. > Compute a version of the measured precision-recall curve with precision monotonically decreasing, by setting the precision for recall r to the maximum precision obtained for *any* recall \(\tilde{r}\geq r\). i.e. given the PR curve in orange, calculate the max precision to the right for all the recall points thus getting a new curve in green.
